title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
statement: Given a sorted array, remove the duplicates in-place such that each element appears only once and returns the new length.

mistakes.hint1: Try to do something like shifting elements when a unique one is found.
mistakes.hint2: Consider using two pointers: one to scan, one to place the unique element.
mistakes.hint3: Think about how you would overwrite the duplicate elements instead of creating a new array.
mistakes.hint4: Keep a `write_index` that only moves forward when you see a number different from the previous one.

mistakes.hint1: Make sure you only increase your counter when you find a unique element.
mistakes.hint2: Are you incrementing the write pointer on duplicates? That defeats the purpose.
mistakes.hint3: Trace your code with [1, 1, 2]. Does your counter become 3?

mistakes.hint2: Is your pointer correctly incrementing to reach the end of the array?
mistakes.hint3: Make sure you aren't accidentally decrementing your loop counter inside the loop.
mistakes.hint4: Ensure your `for` or `while` loop strictly advances `i < n` every iteration.

mistakes.hint1: How does your code behave if the array only has 1 element?
mistakes.hint2: If the array has size 0 or 1, there are no duplicates to remove.
mistakes.hint3: Check if your loop safely skips execution when `n <= 1`.
mistakes.hint4: Add a quick `if (n <= 1) return n;` at the start of your function.

mistakes.hint1: Review the operator you are using to check if two adjacent elements are the same or different.
mistakes.hint2: Are you writing elements when they MATCH instead of when they DIFFER?
mistakes.hint3: If you check `arr[i] == arr[i-1]`, you are storing the duplicates.
